chapter.title: The Commissioning Record That Wasn't
chapter.sub: An amplifier dies, the warranty needs the data, and the record says PASS with nothing behind it — and Maya’s initials on the front.

items.text: SEASON 9 · EPISODE 5 · DRAFT · CASE-049  The MER · Maya, Nkechi (the commissioning agent), Dario and Odile · Level L5 · Advanced support (formulas on request)  An amplifier channel dies. The warranty needs the commissioning data. The record says PASS — and there’s no file. Then Maya finds her own initials.  ⚑ RV-170: the owner accepts the record; warranty terms are the manufacturer’s. RV-172: figures illustrative. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: The Commissioning Record That Wasn't
items.stakes: A dead amplifier channel, a warranty that needs the test data, and a record that says more than was ever tested — with your name on the summary.
items.reward: A record where every line points at its evidence — and a signature you've owned.

objectives.text: Find how much of the record is real
Pick the clues that decide it
Decide what you do about your signature
Decide what a record must be

items.alt: The main equipment room; Nkechi points at an amplifier with a red fault light; Maya holds the thick commissioning record.

bubbles.text: Amp four, channel three. The balcony's silent. The record says PASS.

items.caption: The balcony has a show tonight.

lines.text: Forty-eight lines say PASS. I have thirty files.
Then eighteen of them are words.

items.prompt: 09:10. The balcony zone is silent and the warranty needs data. What happens first?
items.risk: A silent balcony tonight — or a false claim to the manufacturer.
timeout: Tonight's show starts with a silent balcony.

hints.text: What matters tonight, and what proves the record?

options.label: Send the manufacturer the record as it is
options.result: Nkechi: “Not with eighteen tests that never happened.”
options.consequence: Sends a claim you can't stand behind.
options.fail: Never send what you can't stand behind.

options.label: Put the balcony on the spare amplifier channel and test it; then match every PASS line in the record against a test file
options.result: The balcony plays by eleven. By noon: 30 files for 48 lines.
options.consequence: The audience first, then the evidence.

options.label: Retest all 48 channels today and replace the record
options.result: The new record is fine — and the old one, the evidence of what was claimed, is gone.

options.label: Ask Dario to send the missing files
options.consequence: Asks for what may not exist.

items.title: Thirty of forty-eight.
items.body: Thirty test files, spread over five days the week before handover. Eighteen PASS lines with nothing behind them — every one of them exactly the design value, to a tenth of a decibel. Dario pulls the tester's own memory: thirty sessions, not forty-eight. The eighteen were typed on handover eve by the technician who later left the integrator. Real measurements scatter. These didn't.
items.label: Test: how much has no evidence — and why the values give it away.

items.label: **Clue board:** which PASS lines are real?

items.title: Your signature.
items.body: The front page of the record: ‘Commissioning record reviewed — all amplifier channels PASS.’ Initialled M. Timed 03:10 on handover eve. Maya remembers the night — the punch list, the marshal due in the morning, the pen. She remembers signing. She doesn't remember opening page 7.
items.label: Test: the retest time — and what she does about the signature.

items.prompt: 14:10. Nobody has noticed the initials but you. What do you do?
items.risk: A record nobody trusts — including your next signature.
timeout: You wait for someone to ask.
Odile finds it herself on Thursday.

hints.text: What would you want to hear from someone else in your place?

options.label: Say nothing — the technician typed the lines
options.result: True, and the summary still has your name.

options.label: Tell Odile and Nkechi in writing, today: you signed the summary at 03:10 without opening the detail pages. Then the witnessed retest
options.result: Odile: “Thank you for telling me before I found it.” Nkechi books the retest for tomorrow.
options.consequence: Own your part before anyone asks.

options.label: Re-sign the summary with today's date after the retest
options.fail: Never rewrite a record; correct it openly.

options.label: Ask Dario to take the blame for the page
options.consequence: Moves your part onto someone else.

items.title: The test that said perfect
items.body: In 1990 a space telescope reached orbit with a main mirror ground to the wrong shape by about two micrometres. The instrument used to test the mirror during manufacture had been assembled with one lens out of position by about 1.3 millimetres, so the tests said the mirror was perfect. Other checks that disagreed were set aside. A servicing mission fitted corrective optics in 1993. The test was precise. It was measuring the wrong thing.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #86 · AVERY'S LENS  A record is only as true as its evidence  Every line in a record should point at the evidence behind it — and a signature should mean the signer looked.  Forty-eight lines said PASS. Thirty had tests behind them. The summary had Maya's name on it.

items.alt: The commissioning grid after the witnessed retest: all 48 cells linked to a file, two amber cells marking faults found and fixed; re-issued with exceptions listed and accepted by the owner.
items.caption: Every line points at its evidence.

items.title: 30 sessions · 5 days
items.body: The cable-and-amplifier tester's own session list, exported by Dario: 30 sessions over five days the week before handover. Nothing on handover eve.

items.prompt: Friday. What must a record be from now on?
items.risk: The next record that claims more than was tested.
timeout: The lighting record is signed the same way next month.

hints.text: What would have stopped you signing blind at 03:10?

options.label: Signed by two people instead of one
options.result: Two people who don't open the pages.

options.label: Every line links the evidence file behind it; a summary is signed only by someone who opened the files — and says which ones; exceptions are listed, not hidden
options.result: Nkechi writes it into the commissioning standard; Dario's team uses it next week.

options.label: Blame the technician who left
options.result: He did type them. The system let a summary be signed blind.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  A record line is a claim until it links its evidence (% = part ÷ whole × 100 of lines with files). Real measurements scatter; identical design values weren’t measured. Keep the original record as evidence and issue a corrected one; plan the witnessed retest (time = count ÷ rate). If your name is on a summary you didn’t check, say so first, in writing. Sign only what you opened.
REFLECTION (optional)  · What have you signed at 3 a.m. — and would you want someone to open page seven?
